Can you please tell us whether you know when he registered his identity and why he had been registered for nine years as a missing person? Thank you." And your answer was: "Just to go to the top part of your question, I would not say that distant relatives giving DNA samples would be better than those closer relatives giving DNA samples. As for the boy, Witness PW --" and it's written "PW-114" -- "I don't remember when he was first interviewed. I certainly know it was before he testified in 2004. I'd have to find that out to see." I just want to clarify with you: Do you remember giving that answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I just want to clarify something with you, because in your direct testimony at page 7718 through 7719, in respect of the photograph that's now in e-court - I think you can see it - you stated that Ramo Osmanovic was in Sandici Meadow, and you said: "As we've seen on the Petrovic video on July 13th, in the afternoon, in the video footage you'll see him calling out for his son, Nermin." If we can just go into private session for a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, with respect to Ramo Osmanovic and his son, Nermin Osmanovic, you indicated that his son was -- the remains of his son were identified; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know or can you recall where his remains were recovered?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was one of the Hadzici grave-sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I would like to go into private session, please, again and have Exhibit 167 -- P00167 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, you were asked certain questions about information concerning some 500 missing persons that General Tolimir said were being kept on the missing persons list, and that General Tolimir attributed to a person by the name of Tokaca who he said was the president of the Commission for Finding Missing Persons, as it was translated in the record. This is on page 7744 of the transcript. Now, in respect of those 500 individuals, you indicated that you were not very knowledgeable about a particular claim, but what I'd like to ask you about is as follows. If I could have 65 ter 6796 in e-court, please. All right. We'll just wait a second for the English to come up. I see it's there now. What we have here is a publication from the Research and Documentation Centre in Sarajevo. I think you can see the caption there. And it's dated 21 April 2010, and it is entitled "Denial regarding quotes of Mr. Mirsad Tokaca regarding genocide victims in Srebrenica." First, in the question that was put to you by General Tolimir at page 7744 of the transcript -- where he refers to this person named Tokaca, Mirsad Tokaca, as you can see in the document, as the president of the Commission for Finding Missing Persons, were you aware that Mr. Tokaca was the director of the Research and Documentation Centre of Sarajevo and not a president of a missing persons commission?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know what his position was, but I knew it was not as the head of ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, in respect of the first paragraph, it reads that: "In reaction to recent allegations in the press about manipulations of numbers of victims of genocide committed in Srebrenica, the Research and Documentation Centre representatives wish to address the public. In connection with this, a sentence of Mr. Mirsad Tokaca about the victims is often mentioned and quoted, and for this reason, specifically, we wish to make an announcement to the public with additional explanations." Now, in particular, were you aware that the Research and Documentation Centre of Sarajevo had commented on the statements that were attributed to Mirsad Tokaca and, in particular, as referred to in the question put to you by General Tolimir about these 500 missing individuals?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware that the centre had publicly commented on his -- on his comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just take you down to the middle paragraph of this document, and I think a good place to kind of locate everyone is where you can see, in quotes "human losses, 1991 through 1995." And what the sentence reads is: "Thus, in the period 2004 through 2007, in the course of the investigation "Human Losses 1991 through 1995," it was established through check-ups that about 500 persons, who were earlier on various lists registered as missing, were found alive and that they have been eliminated from the list of victims." Now, having been involved in investigations in Srebrenica, in particular the investigation of Srebrenica and Zepa events, do you have any information that individuals that went missing in 1991 through 1994 are included on any missing list, OTP list, concerning the Srebrenica and Zepa events?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me take you down to the last paragraph here, and, in particular, I'll refer you to the first sentence of that paragraph, where it says: "It was stated that the sentence '500 missing persons who were found alive' was taken out of context and presented to the public in a way to create the impression that the list of killed and missing people from Srebrenica still contains 500 persons. First of all, it was published by the SRNA news agency ..." Do you have familiarity with this news agency?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of the agency, I know it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell us about it, if you know.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a local news agency in Bosnia. I can't tell you more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It says. "... the information was taken over by other media mostly from the area of Republika Srpska." And then it says: "With regard to this, Mr. Tokaca made another statement as well when he denied all this in a programme of Hayat TV." Now, given the fact that Mr. Tokaca has denied this and that the 500 people said to be missing has been taken out of context, do you know whether or not any of this had any impact whatsoever on the OTP missing list concerning the individuals from Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- no, I mean I don't. In reading the article that you just showed, it indicates that if -- if this were the case, that they were taken off the list during a certain time-period, and certainly any of the lists that we have consulted, and certainly had consulted with the book, was past that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: One last question, and that is: With respect to determining any impact that this may or may not have had on the OTP missing list, can you tell us who, within the OTP, that this would be appropriately attended to?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume it would be our demographers and, in particular, Ewa Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. That concludes my redirect examination. Mr. President, I would like to offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1370, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, is that the end of the testimony of the Witness Gallagher in this trial or will she be called again?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think that she will be called again on yet another discrete issue, but it does conclude her testimony as concerning this particular part -- this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since a document was introduced in the redirect denying Mr. Tokaca's statement, who was not -- actually, the document was not presented before the examination-in-chief, would you permit me to put a couple of questions relating to this document? This was not in the examination-in-chief or in the redirect -- actually, it wasn't presented in the examination-in-chief or in the cross-examination. The Prosecutor introduced this document just now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There are two things that arise. One is: The general has familiarity with this article. It was dealt with, I believe, in connection with the testimony of Mr. Ruez. That was back on 4th of May, 2010. In particular, it was referred to then, when the general raised at that time the same issue concerning these 500 individuals. The second is that during the course of cross-examination -- well, first, during the course of direct examination, there was no mention made concerning this article or this issue. The general raised this on cross-examination, when he put the following question, and this is at page 7744 of the transcript, beginning there, at line 24, where he says: "Thank you. Did you hear that the president of the Commission for Finding Missing Persons this year, at press conferences, publicly stated that he had established that more than 500 persons were being kept on the missing persons list?" This document is directly responsive to that. He identifies this person as Mr. Tokaca, which is the subject matter of this document. And so this press article, from the agency of which Mr. Tokaca is a director, is directly responsive to the issue raised as to the 500 individuals that General Tolimir says Mr. Tokaca discussed as having been -- having been kept on the missing list, and, in fact, it shows that that's not the case, as was put during the cross-examination. So there's no basis for General Tolimir to conduct a re-cross-examination based on the fact that what he has proffered during the course of cross-examination has been rebutted by a document put in redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the position of both parties. And since the Chamber has the discretion to allow or not to allow additional questions, in these specific circumstances the Chamber will grant the application of the accused to put questions to the witness especially and only to this document just admitted as P1370, because this is a new document which is now in evidence, under these specific circumstances of this case. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I did want to just point out that it's not a new document. The accused has had the document since May of this year, and, in fact, it's specifically referenced in the transcript of the testimony of Mr. Ruez. So I just want -- I just want the Trial Chamber to know that, because I know that although I referred to it being discussed back then, it was actually -- it was actually used to address this specific issue, and the accused has had the document since then as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware of the fact that it was on the 65 ter exhibit list as 65 ter 6796, but it is now today received as an exhibit into evidence. Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber has ruled on it. Please put your questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I would like to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm looking on the clock. We have now a quarter before 6.00. Do you need more than five or ten minutes for your additional questions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But if you would like to take the break now, I'm fine with putting my questions after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, you should proceed now if you only need seven minutes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Further cross-examination by Mr. Tolimir:

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to welcome Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this: This denial issued by the IWC or IVC, does that have anything of what Mr. Tokaca said? Does it quote him in any way or does it state what he said? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me take a quick look at the document. He appears to be more paraphrased than directly quoted, except for in the last paragraph, where it says: "It was stated that the sentence '500 missing persons who were found alive' ..." That's the only part that I see in quotes that was verbatim.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Were -- Mr. Tokaca's words that are being cited, are they cited anywhere in this denial or does the denial contain the words of whoever drafted it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it doesn't appear that he -- that they are citing his specific words, specific sentences. It's a comment, it seems to be, on the content and context of what he had said or any report he had made.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to tell us if the OTP or you have a denial issued by Mr. Tokaca, himself, regarding the things that are being denied by this institution as well and that I'm not aware of? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly don't have a denial issued by him. I do not know what the OTP has regarding him. As I mentioned, I know very little of this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In fact, we do have such a document, and that was disclosed to the accused 10 September 2010. It is a document that is signed by Mirsad Tokaca, and he explains, in effect, what we can see in the article. I think the accused knows this. And if it would be of some assistance to the Trial Chamber, I can present that to the Trial Chamber so that you can evaluate it and take a look at it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you give us a number of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It has an ERN number of 0667-9059.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If the Prosecution has a number -- a document, let them then tender it, because what is in the database with an ERN number doesn't mean that I was actually able to find it in the database and was able to familiarise myself with it. Perhaps the Prosecutor can show it in the courtroom, present it, so that we can see what it is, what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, do you have a 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We don't have a 65 ter number for it, but -- and I'm not sure if we can -- I can put it on the ELMO and we can take a look at it. I have a hard copy of it, but I don't have a 65 ter number for it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the moment, Mr. Tolimir is putting questions. It's up to you, how to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am interested in Ms. Gallagher's answer to this:

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Anything that is connected to this document which was published, this denial, did the Prosecution investigate anything on this matter relating to data you presented here as a witness, that you stand by, and that you answered a question from Judge Mindua previously about a person identifying themselves and in that way being able to be removed from the list? I apologise. It was a question put not by Judge Mindua but by Judge Nyambe. I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think, although I may not be able to find the reference immediately, that this question was put to Ms. Gallagher on cross-examination already as concerns the investigation concerning these individuals or the source of that information, and she's answered it. And I don't know that it arises from the redirect examination that was conducted just a few moments ago. In any event, I should inform the Court that the document that I'm referring to has been available to the accused for some time. It will be dealt with appropriately by the demographers that the Prosecution intends to call, which I think -- whom I think will be able to answer these questions more effectively and more informatively for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber gave you the possibility to put some more questions, but only related to the document we have on the screen, not to other issues. Do you have any more questions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't have questions, and I don't wish to put any other questions other than ones that have to do with the document. I only want to ask this: Ms. Gallagher, who stands by this data, does she stand behind this data or do the demographers stand behind this data? Because on a number of occasions during the cross-examination, she said that this is something that the demographers can identify, but we're talking about 33 persons who had been identified, 28 of whom on the basis of DNA. This is why I'm asking. Who is standing behind this data? Is it Ms. Gallagher or is it the persons who were the source of these documents? I would need to know this in order to be able to present documents that can prove the opposite. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this could have been part of your cross-examination. This question has nothing to do with the article we have on the screen, and, therefore, this is not an appropriate question for this witness at this point in time. I take it that you have finished your additional questioning for the witness. If there are no other questions by the Chamber, I would like to thank you, Ms. Gallagher, for your attendance again here in the courtroom, and you are free now to return to your normal work. Thank you very much again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, what are your plans for tonight, for the last part of this session?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have another witness, Mr. Janc, who I believe is prepared to go. I just started my redirect examination of him on the specific issue concerning the Skorpions video, the involvement of the Serbian MUP with the VRS and so on, as you may recall, and I'm prepared to go forward with that, with the Court's leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, we will do that and use every minute of our trial time. We must have our second break now, and we will resume half past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Janc. Before your examination will continue, the Chamber would like to discuss the next witness especially with Mr. McCloskey. In the meantime, we have received a list of about 30 documents to be used with Mr. Blaszczyk. There are some concerns about this list. These -- I think we only found two of these exhibits on the 65 ter witness list. These are not even indicated with these 65 ter numbers. We see that all these documents, many of them are indicated to be note-books of Ratko Mladic. In this case, we are not prepared to accept testimony of Mr. Blaszczyk on this amount of documents. Only four documents related to the Mladic note-books are on the 65 ter exhibit list. These are 65 ter 5486, 87, 88 and 89. Two of them we were able to find now on the new list of documents to be used with Mr. Blaszczyk. This is not an appropriate way to introduce a witness. We have not received a witness summary for this witness, only by e-mail an indication that Mr. Blaszczyk will testify about the chain of custody of the Mladic note-books. We end about the authenticity of these note-books. Comparing the list of the documents already in the 65 ter exhibit list, they are called "Mladic note-books," two of them. In the new list, they are called "Brown business diary," with the same number. We have no indication about the content. We have no indication about the content of the witness testimony to be heard tomorrow, and, therefore, we are not in the position to accept testimony of Mr. Blaszczyk on those topics not yet in the 65 ter witness list. We would like to invite the Prosecution to file a written submission to grant the addition of these documents to the 65 ter witness list. If we receive such a motion, we will -- with a response by the Defence, I think this is a principle of fairness, even if the Defence is in the possession of these documents already, but were obviously not aware of the fact that Mr. Blaszczyk will testify about these matters. Only the four note-books listed in the 65 ter exhibit list - I've mentioned their numbers - may be the content of the testimony of Mr. Blaszczyk viva voce to be commenced tomorrow. I hope I made the position of the Chamber clear. Are there any comments by the parties? Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. We understand, Mr. President, and this was, as you know, was an effort to try to fill some space on what isn't as complicated as it seems, but it is an important topic and it deserves the attention you would like to have it given. And we will get that prepared and file it properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you intend to call Mr. Blaszczyk to testify about the four documents listed in the 65 ter exhibit list?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It probably would be more efficient to get it all together so that this can be done at once. Fundamentally, he will be testifying to what he testified to in the Karadzic case. So I have not had time, myself, to review that in any detail, but I can just -- so you understand a bit what this was about, again I'll stand like this. In 2008, the Serbians did a search, received some Mladic diaries. They did one much more recently and they've -- we now have a collection that covers most of the war period. And I'm sure you've heard other trials are dealing with these diaries, because many of the entries in the diaries have certain relevance to all these other trials, and so fundamentally this is not much different than what he was testifying about the Drina Corps collection, that this is when the -- this is how the Serbian forces went and did these searches, and they found a lot of material. And then in addition to that, he provides some material that helps -- will help in any evaluation regarding their genuineness. For example, if there's a reference in one of the diaries about a meeting from the Serbian Assembly, and then they find -- and then I think we've attached the Serbian Assembly, that it would show a similar entry. Mr. Blaszczyk is not an analyst nor an expert, he wasn't going to talk about all this, but he's just providing the background for it. So here's all the materials that they got over the years, here is how it happened, and here's some other material that will help the Court, should they want to review this material in analysing it. And it came in relatively simply that way, and -- but it should be explained to you properly so that you're not wondering what it is that were happening before it happens. And we'll suffer the unfortunate problem of not having a witness tomorrow, but I think it's better that you are more comfortable that you're getting a proper presentation of new material, because this is material that's come in, you know, well after the 65 ter list, so we're all -- it's not so essential for this case, but it's something we want you to see, and so we have been getting to it in our -- in a proper time-frame. And we're just trying to accelerate it, but it's not going to work, we can see that, so we'll get it in a better time-frame and get it to you in a motion package that you're more comfortable with. But that's what it's about: He's just going to talk about the searches and what was obtained in the searches, but it gets more complicated after that. But, in any event, we completely understand your situation, and we'll get it done properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Chamber appreciates your efforts not to use court time and not to lose court time. This is, indeed, a very important matter. On the other hand, we have to be sure that we follow procedure which is according to our Rules of Procedure and Evidence and the normal proceedings in this Tribunal. Are there any further comments? Otherwise, we should continue with the testimony of Mr. Janc. Mr. Janc, welcome back to the courtroom. I have to remind you that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your testimony still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I think we are still in the re-examination by Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Good evening to you and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think when we left of last time, we were looking at 65 ter 6779. If we could have that in e-court, please, and we should not broadcast this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just to reacquaint you with where we are in the process,

utterances.speaker: MR. JANC
utterances.text: I had you on redirect examination concerning the very specific issues raised on cross-examination with regard to your testimony about the authentification [sic] -- "authentication," I should say, of the Skorpion videos, you'll recall. And, in particular, you were asked certain questions regarding the materials that you relied on in the context of your testimony by General Tolimir. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And to be more particular, on page 7034, lines 10 through 23, you were put the following question by General Tolimir. In particular, he says: "We're still talking about information concerning the executions of these six persons in Trnovo. I won't mention their names. Did you personally investigate how they ended up in Trnovo, which is 200 kilometres away from Srebrenica?" Your answer was: "Not me, personally, but several steps towards this -- regarding this issue have been done by the other members of the OTP, investigators, my colleagues, and there was a statement of one of the individuals who was interviewed, who says that these individuals -- not only this but some other individuals were brought from the area of Srebrenica, after the fall of Srebrenica, by buses and trucks to Trnovo, to the Trnovo area. These buses and trucks were going up and down several times and were bringing the men from Srebrenica down to this area, and these six individuals, those who were the last group of those transported down from Srebrenica and were subsequently killed there." Do you recall giving that answer to the preceding question?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The statement we have now in e-court, is that one of the statements that you relied upon in giving that answer and in making these assertions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is take you over to page 11 in this document. I think -- I just want to see if I can get the corresponding page in the B/C/S. It looks like it should also be page 11 in the B/C/S. No, it will be page 12 in the B/C/S, I think. In the English, I would direct your attention, in particular, to the sentence that begins: "The operation in Trnovo was going on for some 18 to 19 days." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. It's the third paragraph down on the page, for the Trial Chamber's benefit. In the fifth paragraph, we see that this individual states that: "After I had left --" All right. I understand it should be page 11 in the B/C/S. It may cross over into page 12. I can't tell just now. But, in any event, in the English, it reads: "After I had left, Slobodan Medic ordered aka Coke to prepare the trucks and buses. Two men, aka Braco and Djuro Meleusic, were ordered to take a bus and truck and to go to Srebrenica." Did you hear that or did you consider that in making the conclusions that you did during the course of your cross-examination testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we go a little bit further down - it should be the second paragraph from the bottom - this individuals states: "With the bus and the truck, they were driving back and forth to Srebrenica, bringing captured Muslims from Srebrenica to different locations to be killed. I do not know exactly where in the Srebrenica area they picked up the people, but they always went to the same location." Did that form the basis of your testimony as you gave it during cross-examination as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in particular, in the very last paragraph, it states that: "Slobodan Medic knew that none of the groups was for us but he told the men that this package was for us. The word 'package' was always used to describe a group of prisoners." And then it says: "Medic singled out the men who should kill the prisoners, and he issued the orders, and the men were taken away and killed." Is this part of the information that you relied on also in terms of your testimony as you gave it during cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd just like to go to the next page in the English, and I think it may -- it may be the next page also in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And right at the top of the page in English, you can see it says: "I learned about this incident because I was given a copy of the videotape shot during the killing." Do you -- you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this part of the information that you relied on in order to authenticate the videotape in question?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I'd like to do -- if you recall, during the course of your redirect testimony when you were last year, an issue arose with respect to the association of the Skorpions unit and what was referred to as the Serbian DB. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you rely also on this particular statement in terms of your testimony concerning the existence of such an association?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also on this statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd just like to briefly show you page 7 of this statement in the English. I think it should be -- what is written, anyway, is page 7 in the B/C/S. If you look at the bottom of the page, I can tell you how far we have to go. I think we're there. Yes, we'll have to go from page -- I'm sorry. We'll have to go from page 6 to page 7, so we'll start with page 6, please. All right. In the English -- I'm sorry, at page 6 in the English. Yes, we are there. You can see that this individual is talking about having joined the unit in 1994. That's right in the middle of the page. Do you see that, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go to page 7, I think, on both documents -- yeah, I think that's right. In the middle of the page in the English, you'll see that it says: "The Skorpions were wearing green camouflage uniforms, similar to the ones Arkan's unit was wearing. We had a badge with a sword showing that we were a Serbian DB unit. Under the sword was written the words 'Skorpion' and the sword was the insignia of the Serbian DB." Are you familiar with that particular badge or patch?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've seen this badge once, but right now I would not be able to recall it, how it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go down to the following paragraph, which begins: "After the Skorpions were disbanded ..." It reads: "... some of the members were given a document telling that they were a reserve force of the Special Unit of the Serbian DB, known as the JSO." Can you tell us a little bit about that, if you relied on that concerning your testimony about the association of the Skorpions unit and the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you -- I think I'm done with this document for now. It's 65 ter 6779. Mr. President, I would offer this for admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1371, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it should be under seal. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness 65 ter 6780, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, is this a statement that you also considered in terms of your testimony regarding the authenticity of the Skorpions video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you may recall that this is an individual who is referred to in the affidavit of Tore Soldal, the OTP investigator, that's in evidence now. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I'd like to take you to -- bear with me for one moment. I'd like to take you to paragraph 105 of this statement. And I don't have a B/C/S page number handy, I don't think, but if we can go to -- well, you've got it. Thank you very much. If you look at paragraph 105, there is a reference in this statement that this individual went to see someone by the name of Boca. Do you know this person Boca, who that is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this individual is a member of the Skorpions unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Could it have been Slobodan Medic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And this individual says that: "When I went to see him, I saw a bus full of civilians arrive, escorted by the CSB. These civilians were from Srebrenica. The CSB people called Boca out and removed the civilians from the bus. Boca asked what was going on, and he was told that these civilians were 'our share.' The CSB man explained to him that they were distributing civilians for killing in different locations because they didn't want too many people killed in one place." Did you take account of this particular paragraph, this reference in this statement, in terms of -- in terms of establishing the authenticity of the videotape, the Skorpions videotape?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You will realise we're running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have no idea how much time you need for concluding your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have really -- well, I have one other statement that I'd like the witness to take a look at, and I don't think it will take much longer than how long it's taken with this statement, so maybe another five minutes. But I can also -- as you know, this witness is available on relatively short notice, and we are in the midst of this examination, so it will be easy to pick up if you prefer to adjourn now. I see that we've already over the time, so that might be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is always a problem for the whole staff, for the interpreters, for the Transportation Unit, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just -- I think I'm finished with this document. I would offer it into evidence, and then that will be it for today. And hopefully I can pick up, at the convenience of the Trial Chamber, on another day or time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1372, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When did you intend to call Mr. Janc again for continuation of his re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can call him whenever it's convenient for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that Mr. Blaszczyk will not testify tomorrow. There is no other witness tomorrow, and therefore I think for continuation for another 10 or 15 minutes, it is especially in the interests of the accused not to be transported for this short period from the UNDU to the Tribunal, that in that case it's not very helpful to sit tomorrow at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If that's the case, Mr. President, Mr. Janc can be scheduled whenever it is convenient for the Court. Other than that, next week sometime, or any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, would you agree with that, not to sit tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I agree with that proposal if, indeed, it is only a quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, we have to adjourn now and resume on Monday in the afternoon at 2.15 in this courtroom. Thank you very much.
